    - Ruan. Captain of the Cliff Watch, ten years. Grew up above the Long Stair. Joined at eighteen, when the watch was old men and boys.
    - Now it is a dozen guards and not enough nights. That is the job.
    - You asked before. Here is the rest. Three winters back the first one came up the face, not down the paths. Moira rang the bar. Torva and two of hers drove it over the edge.
    - I held the lantern while Elspeth stitched Torva's jaw. Have not told that to many. You have steady hands. Keep them.
    - We stand the high landings, where the forest paths reach the top. Walk the stairs at night with lanterns. Ring the iron bar at the head of the Long Stair when something comes.
    - Same work. The high landings, the stairs at night, the bar at the head of the Long Stair. Difference is Gunna's lanterns on the landings now. They burn steady in any wind.
    - I test every rope on the cliffs once a month. Hang my whole weight off it. Kestra's I test twice. She hates that. Rope still holds.
    - The roads in from Gorse Downs and the Saltwood are quieter since you walked them. Less coming down to the stairs from that side. Good. One side fewer.
    - They come up the face now. At night. Always where it is darkest. I want a lantern on every high landing. Gunna says a good lantern cannot be hurried.
    - Tarran says brighter, sooner. I have not said no. Things coming down from the forest I understand. Things coming up from the sea are something else.
    - Lanterns help. The climbers find the stretches between them. Moira saw that first. Or she thinks she did.
    - People have brought me things they told no one else. I want to be sure before it goes to Iska. I am afraid sure will come too late.
